I can't even focus on fixing the bug because I'm too busy grieving a future that hasn't even happened yet.

My dad called today to ask how my midterms went and I lied and told him I got an A when I actually got a D on the engineering math paper. I couldn't bear to hear his voice drop or have him bring up my cousin who just got into an Ivy League. Now I'm sitting in the library stare-blanking at the next syllabus, completely paralyzed because if I study and still fail the end-sem, it means I’m actually just stupid and have no excuses left.

I didn't submit my final project draft for the AI/ML course even though it was 90% done because I kept convinced myself it was complete garbage. I stayed up till 4 AM staring at the 'Submit' button, and my mind just kept telling me that the professor would look at my model's low accuracy and realize I'm a complete fraud who doesn't belong in this department. I literally preferred taking a zero over risking someone seeing me try and fail.

Everyone in our hostel WhatsApp group is talking about their summer internship shortlists and comparing stipend amounts. I haven't even cleared the first round of a single coding test, and every time I see a new 'Congratulations' post, my chest gets so tight I can barely breathe. I feel like an absolute loser who is destined to end up unemployed while my friends move to Bangalore and start their lives without me.

I have a viva exam with an external evaluator tomorrow and I'm already planning to pretend I have a high fever so I can skip it and take the backlog exam next semester. Just the thought of him asking me a concept I don't know and staring at me in silence while I stumble over my words makes me want to crawl into a hole. I'd rather destroy my GPA than face the humiliation of looking stupid for ten minutes.

I just stared at the screen for two hours during the mock DSA round and couldn't even optimize a simple sliding window problem. Everyone in the batch is posting their LeetCode milestones and I'm sitting here with two active backlogs thinking I'm going to end up unplaced. My dad keeps asking about the mock results and I lied, telling him the server crashed. I feel like a complete imposter who doesn't deserve to be in this department.

My CGPA dropped to 6.8 this semester and I can't breathe. My parents took out a massive loan for this private university, and every time my mom calls to ask if I've started preparing for the TCS or Infosys mass recruitments, my stomach drops. I spent the entire afternoon staring at my resume, literally shaking, because I have nothing to show for these three years except a bunch of half-baked projects that don't even compile. I'm going to fail them, and everyone is going to see I was never smart enough to be here.

Tomorrow is the embedded systems lab viva and the professor is notorious for insulting students in front of the whole class if they can't explain the register mapping. I literally threw up in the bathroom an hour ago because I couldn't remember a single assembly instruction. I'm so terrified of freezing in front of everyone and having him tell me I'm useless. I just want to switch off my phone, hide under my blanket, and never show up to college again.

Every time I open LinkedIn, my feed is filled with 'I'm happy to share that I have secured an internship at Amazon/Microsoft' with some insane package. I couldn't even clear the first round of a local startup's recruitment drive because I panicked during the live debugging session. I feel like a complete failure compared to my roommates who are already discussing their joining dates and signing bonuses. I'm literally going to end up unemployed while everyone else moves to Bangalore and starts their lives.

I just got rejected from the third placement interview in a row. The interviewer asked me a simple SQL query and my mind went totally blank; I couldn't even write a basic JOIN statement. I've spent the last six months studying system design and DBMS, but the second I sit in that hot seat, I sabotage myself. I've started avoiding my friends' calls because they keep asking 'what happened?' and I'm tired of seeing the pity in their eyes. I don't think I'm cut out for this industry.

My dad called today to tell me our neighbor's son got a 14 LPA offer at a fintech company, and then he just sighed and asked how my DSA prep is going. I literally closed my IDE and stared at the wall for two hours because every time I try to run my code and see 'Time Limit Exceeded' or 'Wrong Answer', my stomach violently drops. I feel like an absolute fraud who's going to end up unplaced, wasting all the money they spent on my coaching fees. I can't sleep because my mind just plays a loop of me failing the coding round in front of the interviewer.

I have my semester exams starting next week and I still have two active backlogs from last year. I try to open my book but my hands start shaking and I get so dizzy that I just shut it and go back to sleep. I'm so terrified of failing again and having to tell my friends why I can't graduate on time with them. Everyone else is sharing their mock test scores on the class WhatsApp group and I'm just sitting here paralyzed, waiting for the disaster to happen.

We have our external viva tomorrow for the web dev lab, and my mind is completely blank. I know the concepts, but the moment the professor asks me a question, my voice hitches and I forget basic terms, making me look like a total idiot who paid someone else to write their project. I'm so scared of seeing that disappointed, condescending look on the professor's face when I stutter. I'd honestly rather fake being sick and skip the exam than face that public humiliation.

I somehow got selected for this high-paying summer internship, but instead of being happy, I've spent the last three days throwing up from anxiety. I keep looking at the onboarding docs and I don't understand half of the tech stack they use. They're going to realize they made a huge mistake hiring me, and I'll be exposed as a complete fake during the first standup meeting. The pressure is so suffocating that I'm seriously considering emailing HR to decline the offer before they have the chance to fire me.

In school, I was always the top student, but here in college, I got a C- on my first midterm and I haven't been able to face my parents since. Every time my mom asks how my grades are, I lie and say they haven't been released yet because I'm terrified they'll realize their 'genius' kid is actually mediocre. I can't even start the next assignment because my mind tells me that if I try my best and still fail, it proves I was never actually smart to begin with. I'm just hiding in my hostel room, dodging calls, and feeling like a complete failure.

I messed up a basic linked list traversal during a mock interview today and just stared at the screen while the interviewer sighed. My dad keeps sending me screenshot updates of Sharma ji's son getting 24 LPA at Amazon, and I can't even get past a preliminary screening. I feel like my chest is collapsing under the weight of this impending failure, like I'm a fraud who memorized code but can't think for myself.

The grade sheet for the midterms got posted on the bulletin board and my CGPA has dropped to 6.2. I have two pending lab backlogs and I can't even bring myself to open the IDE anymore without my hands shaking. I’m so terrified of failing the next semester that I've started faking being sick just to avoid going to the lab.

Every single time I open LinkedIn, there's another 'I am thrilled to announce' post from some peer in my batch getting summer internships. Meanwhile, I got rejected from three startup roles this morning and my prep is in shambles. I feel like an absolute loser who's going to end up unemployed while everyone else flies off to their high-paying corporate lives.

We have the external viva tomorrow for our major project and I’m literally dry-heaving in the washroom. What if the examiner asks me a question about our database architecture and my mind just goes completely blank? My teammates worked so hard, and I am terrified that my stupidity is going to ruin their grades along with mine.

My mom called today and asked if I'm even studying because our neighbor's daughter cleared the UPSC prelims. I didn't have the heart to tell her I failed my end-sem DSA lab exam last week and might have to write a supplementary paper. I feel like a total disappointment, like I’m wasting their hard-earned money and will never be the successful child they wanted.
